frontMatter.welcome:
Welcome to the vibrant world of Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, where innovation meets tradition, and excellence is our standard. As you embark on this exciting journey with us, you step into a realm where the rich heritage of India's largest jute conglomerate converges with a forward-looking vision of global success.
At Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, we take immense pride in our roots, deeply embedded in the jute industry, employing a workforce of 18,000 across four thriving jute mills. Our commitment to complete vertical integration, spanning from the cultivation of jute fibers to the crafting of exquisite finished bags in jute fabrics, sets us apart as industry leaders in quality and sustainability.
With a monumental manufacturing capacity of 500 metric tons of jute products churned out daily, our reach extends far beyond borders to over 50 countries worldwide. This international presence underscores our dedication to sharing the timeless allure and eco-friendly essence of jute with a global audience.
Delve into our world where tradition meets transformation, where the rhythmic spin of high-quality yarns intertwines with cutting-edge weaving techniques to create lightweight, finely textured fabrics that stand as testaments to craftsmanship and innovation. Every thread we weave, every design we unveil, speaks volumes of our unwavering commitment to excellence and customer satisfaction.
In the heart of Shaktigarh Jute Park, West Bengal, our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility stands tall as a beacon of progress and ingenuity, where tradition is preserved, and innovation thrives. Here, meticulous craftsmanship and pioneering research blend seamlessly to produce jute products that embody elegance, durability, and the spirit of sustainable luxury.

chapters.title: Social Accountability Policy
chapters.text:
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd is steadfast in its commitment to upholding the rights of workers, enhancing labor conditions, and fostering exemplary social performance both within the organization and in all its stakeholder partnerships and relationships.
## Compliance with Laws and Industry Standards:
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd unwaveringly complies with local, national, and all other applicable laws as well as prevailing industry standards to ensure the highest standards of social accountability.
Child Labor:
Since its inception, Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd has steadfastly adhered to the practice of not engaging workers under the age of 18 in its workforce, ensuring that young individuals are not employed in its operations.
## Forced or Compulsory Labor:
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd unequivocally denounces the use of forced or compulsory labor, ensuring that its workforce operates voluntarily and without the threat of punishment or coercion.

chapters.title: Health and Safety:
chapters.text:
The company is deeply committed to providing a healthy and safe working environment for all personnel employed or contracted, prioritizing the well-being of its workforce.
## Freedom of Association:
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd fully respects and supports the right to freedom of association, ensuring that workers and their organizations are not subjected to any form of discrimination within the workplace.

chapters.title: Non-Discrimination:
chapters.text:
In alignment with its code of conduct, Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd provides equal opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without any form of discrimination. The company also implements positive discrimination in favor of socially disadvantaged communities, provided that potential employees meet merit-based criteria.
## Disciplinary Practices:
All personnel at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd are treated with dignity and respect, and any disciplinary actions taken are in strict accordance with the established laws and regulations.
## Security Practices:
The company diligently ensures the security of its personnel, always giving due regard to human rights under all circumstances.
## Working Hours and Compensation Practices:
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd meticulously adheres to all applicable laws and industry standards regarding working hours, and ensures that its workforce is remunerated with wages meeting or surpassing the minimum wage as stipulated by law.
## Supply Chain Practices:
The company actively promotes human rights practices in its supply chain through various engagement forums, training, surveys, third-party audits, and the inclusion of human rights criteria in its vendor registration process.
## Management System and Grievance Redressal:
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd maintains an effective management system to continuously track its human rights and social performance, judiciously addressing any complaints or grievances to further enhance its systems and processes.
Collective Bargaining and Young Worker Practices:
Workers at Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd hold the right to join collective bargaining organizations, empowering them to have a voice in shaping their working conditions. The company also refrains from engaging workers under the age of 18 within its workforce premises, upholding its commitment to responsible labor practices.
## NGO Agreements:
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd proactively enters into agreements with non-governmental organizations to handle pertinent cases, reinforcing its dedication to ethical and socially responsible practices.
In summary, Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd is resolute in fostering an environment of fairness, respect, and social accountability, where the rights and well-being of its workforce are upheld as paramount.
## Quality, Environment, Health & Safety Policy
At Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd, a reputable manufacturer of Oils and Chemicals Solutions in India's private sector, we are deeply committed to enhancing customer satisfaction through consistent delivery of high-quality products that meet present and future needs, while perpetually advancing our environmental, health, and safety standards across our processes, products, and services.
## We are firmly committed to:
Compliance with Applicable Regulations: We pledge to comply with all relevant legal and other requirements related to quality, environment, health, and safety, ensuring steadfast adherence to established standards.
- Environmental Protection and Pollution Prevention: We are dedicated to preserving the environment and preventing environmental pollution by:
- Striving to reduce and conserve the use of natural resources such as electricity, water, and steam wherever feasible.
- Emphasizing the reduction, recycling, and reuse of waste materials whenever possible.
- Minimizing local pollution and its impact on biodiversity through the adoption of state-of-the-art technology, continuous monitoring, and stringent control measures to manage local environmental pollution.
- Implementing a product life cycle approach throughout the entire supply chain.
- Ensuring no complaints from external stakeholders concerning operational environmental impact.
- Safe and Healthy Working Conditions: We are committed to providing safe and healthy working conditions to prevent work-related injuries and ill health for all involved parties by:
- Identifying and mitigating health and safety hazards and risks through regular medical check-ups, inspection of safety equipment, provision of suitable personal protective equipment (PPE) at the workplace, and continuous monitoring of workplace conditions.
- Promoting awareness of workplace safety through comprehensive training, effective communication, motivation, and soliciting the consultation and participation of employees.
- Controlling and eliminating business and process risks, and capitalizing on opportunities.
- Defining and communicating objectives, targets, and strategies to ensure the adequacy of necessary resources.
- Embracing and promoting a process approach and a risk-based thinking concept within the organization.
- Reinforcing our commitment to sustainable development by effectively implementing and monitoring our Quality, Environment, Health & Safety (QEHS) Management System.

chapters.title: Training and Awareness
chapters.text:
- All employees and non-employee workers receive mandatory training on chemical safety, PPE usage, spill response, and emergency handling.
- Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are readily available at all points where chemicals are used or stored.
## Emergency Procedures
- Clear spill containment procedures and availability of spill kits at designated locations.
- Emergency showers and eye-wash stations are accessible in relevant departments.
- Incident reporting protocols ensure quick action and prevention of recurrence.
## Health & Safety Actions for Non-Employee Workers
- Justify Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd. ensures that non-employee workers—including contractors, temporary staff, vendors, and visitors—are equally protected from workplace hazards.
## Mandatory Safety Induction
- All non-employee workers receive a safety briefing upon entry to the premises, covering chemical hazards, safe work zones, PPE requirements, and emergency procedures.
## Access to PPE and Safety Equipment
- Contractors and third-party workers are provided with appropriate PPE and instructed on its correct usage before starting any task.
## Inclusion in Risk Assessments
- Health and safety risk assessments include activities performed by external workers, ensuring that all hazards associated with contract work are identified and controlled.
## Medical Surveillance for High-Risk Roles
- Contract workers involved in chemical handling, maintenance, or operational tasks participate in health check-ups similar to company employees, when required by job risk levels.
## Emergency Response Involvement
- Non-employee workers are included in evacuation drills, emergency instructions, and communication channels to ensure full preparedness.
## Monitoring and Compliance
- Supervisors and the EHS team regularly monitor contractor activities to ensure adherence to safety rules and report any unsafe behaviors or conditions.
- Communication and Implementation: This policy is comprehensively communicated and explained to the entire organization, disseminated at various levels of the company via placement in different communication areas, and made available to interested parties.
- Reporting an Incident: In the event of any safety incidents, employees are encouraged to immediately report to their supervisor or directly to the designated safety officer or Human Resources department. The company provides a dedicated hotline number and email for incident reporting, ensuring confidentiality and prompt attention to safety concerns.
- Documentation and Incident Investigation Process: We have a meticulous incident reporting, investigation, and review process that involves initial assessment, formal investigation, report preparation, review, implementation, monitoring, and continuous improvement, underscoring our commitment to maintaining a culture of safety and proactive risk management.
- Confidentiality and Non-Retaliation: The company upholds the confidentiality of incident reporting and strictly prohibits any form of retaliation against employees who report incidents, ensuring a safe environment for open communication and continuous improvement.
- Review and Continuous Improvement: We regularly review incident findings in safety committee meetings, incorporating feedback from staff and stakeholders to continually enhance our safety policies and procedures, promoting a culture of continuous feedback and improvement.
- Approval and Implementation: The final policy updates are presented for approval at the Annual General Meeting of the Safety Committee, following which they are communicated to all employees via various channels, with training sessions scheduled where necessary to address significant changes.
- Feedback Mechanism for Continuous Input: We maintain an online platform for continuous feedback and review monthly feedback through regular safety committee meetings, ensuring that employees’ input is incorporated into our safety practices.
By clearly outlining our commitment to quality, environmental protection, health, and safety, and detailing our incident reporting and investigation processes, Jutify Lifestyle Pvt Ltd endeavors to foster a culture of safety, responsibility, and continuous improvement, ensuring the well-being of our workforce and the sustainability of our operations.

## Compensation and Annual Revision Policy
A well-designed compensation and benefits system is essential for attracting, rewarding, and retaining high-quality talent. As Jutify Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd. continues to scale its operations across India, it is critical to maintain a competitive compensation framework that reflects our commitment to fairness, transparency, and performance-driven growth.
Our compensation philosophy recognizes that employees are the foundation of our competitive advantage. Effectively managing our workforce enables us to remain differentiated, agile, and successful in a dynamic business environment.
## Compensation Philosophy
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd. ensures that employee remuneration:
- Complies with all statutory and regulatory requirements
- Meets or exceeds applicable minimum wage standards
- Reflects fair, merit-based compensation
- Is competitive within the industry and relevant markets
Pay structures and annual revisions consider the company’s financial health, economic conditions, market trends, competitor benchmarks, and individual performance.
## Factors Considered for Compensation Structuring
Compensation for each role is determined based on the following parameters:
- Strategic importance of the role
- Scope and complexity of responsibilities
- Performance outcomes and role-specific deliverables
- Relevant prior experience
- Functional and behavioural competencies
- Educational qualifications
- Availability of talent in the job market
- Industry and competitor pay benchmarks
- Internal parity and fairness
- Geographical cost-of-living considerations
## Compensation Structure
Employee compensation consists of Fixed Pay and Variable Pay components, depending on the position level.

chapters.title: Career Development
chapters.text:
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd. is committed to providing all employees with structured, fair, and merit-based career development opportunities. Promotions and career progression are determined through ongoing assessments, performance evaluations, and demonstrated readiness for expanded responsibilities. Our focus is to ensure that every employee has the opportunity to grow professionally in a transparent and unbiased manner.
## Promotion Criteria
Promotion to the next career level is based on a comprehensive assessment of:
- Performance ratings from previous appraisal cycles
- Overall conduct, behaviour, and adherence to company values
- Consistent compliance with safety protocols
- Feedback and evaluations from supervisors and department heads
- Availability of a suitable higher-level role within the organization
Promotion decisions are typically reviewed during the annual increment cycle, where employee performance and achievements are assessed collectively. All promotion or revision approvals rest with the Senior Leadership Team or Management.
## Fair & Non-Discriminatory Advancement
Career growth opportunities are provided in a fair, unbiased, and transparent manner. No employee will be denied career advancement on the basis of any non-merit factor such as gender, caste, religion, ethnicity, disability, age, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic. Decisions are strictly merit-driven and performance-based.
## Role Movement & Transitions
Jutify Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd. actively supports internal mobility as a way to strengthen employee capabilities and meet evolving organizational needs. Role movements may be vertical, horizontal, geographical, or transversal, depending on the nature of the opportunity and employee readiness.
## Types of Internal Mobility
## Vertical Mobility
Movement to a higher-level role based on strong performance, capability, leadership potential, and readiness. This includes promotions and upward transitions within a career path.
## Horizontal Mobility
Movement within the same job level to a different department or function. This supports skill diversification and broad exposure across the organization—for example, shifts from production to quality, or from HR to administration.
## Geographical Mobility
Movement from one work location to another (where applicable), including permanent transfers, temporary assignments, or roles at new sites. This may occur based on project needs, employee capability, or organizational expansion.
## Transversal Mobility
Movement across different job families or functional roles based on transferable skills. This includes role transitions that involve cross-skilling, exploring new functions, or developing multi-disciplinary capabilities.
## nternal Hiring & Opportunities
To maximize internal talent and encourage long-term careers, Jutify Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd. prioritizes internal candidates before external recruitment. Employees are encouraged to explore open positions within the organization.
## nternal Job Posting (IJP) Process
- All available roles are communicated internally through official HR channels such as email, notice boards, or internal communication platforms.
- Employees can apply for roles that align with their skills, qualifications, and career aspirations.
- Applications are evaluated by HR and relevant department heads transparently and fairly.
## Communication of Movement & Decisions
- All promotions, transfers, role changes, and internal selections are documented and communicated formally to employees.
- HR maintains detailed records of internal hiring decisions, approvals, and evaluations to ensure process transparency and compliance.
## nternal Talent Mapping & Marketplace
HR maintains an internal skills database that tracks:
- Employee capabilities
- Certifications and training
- Performance records
- Talent potential
This enables the organization to match employees to roles, projects, or opportunities that best fit their competencies and career goals.
## Employee Growth Programs
To strengthen internal mobility and career progression, Jutify Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd. implements several development-oriented programs that equip employees for future roles.
## Job Shadowing Program
Employees may observe and learn from colleagues in different roles to:
- Understand job expectations
- Learn new skills
- Explore alternative career paths
- Prepare for future role transitions
Shadowing assignments are recorded and monitored by HR.
## Job Rotation & Job Swaps
Departments may rotate employees across functions or tasks to:
- Enhance skill breadth
- Reduce dependency on specific individuals
- Build operational resilience
- Support succession planning
Job swaps may occur between employees of similar roles to support cross-learning.
## Mentoring & Sponsorship Programs
High-performing or high-potential employees may be paired with mentors or senior leaders who provide:
- Career guidance
- Performance coaching
- Skill development support

chapters.title: Leave Policy
chapters.text:
## Privilege Leave (Pl):
- PL Entitlement: Employees are entitled to 20 days of Paid Leave (PL) per year.
- Carry Forward Limit: Employees may carry forward up to 30 days of PL each year, not including the current year's entitlement.
- Leave Encashment: Any accumulated PL exceeding 50 days can be encashed during the service period. All remaining PL will be encashed at the time of resignation, retirement, or separation, based on the last drawn basic salary.
- Leave Credit: PL will be credited at the start of each year. For employees joining after January 1st, PL will be credited on a pro-rata basis. Other terms and conditions will apply as per the Factory Act.
- Excess Leave Utilization: If an employee leaves the organization after using more PL than entitled, the excess amount will be deducted from their gross salary.
- Leave Usage Rules: PL can be taken up to 5 times in a year, with a minimum of 1 day per application. For 3 or more days of PL, employees must apply at least one week in advance.
- Leave Clubbing: PL cannot be combined with Casual Leave (CL), Sick Leave (SL), Paternity Leave, or Compensatory Off (C-off).
- Intervening Days Off: Any weekly off days or paid holidays that occur during the PL period will not count as part of the PL.
## Sick Leave (SL)
- Leave Entitlement: Employees are entitled to 10 days of Sick Leave (SL) per year.
- Carry Forward Limit: Employees can carry forward a maximum of 20 days of SL each year, excluding the current year's entitlement.
- Leave Encashment: There is no provision for encashing SL.
- Leave Lapse: Any SL accumulated beyond 20 days will be forfeited.
- Leave Credit: SL will be credited at the start of each year.
- Pro-Rata Credit: Employees who join after January 1st will receive SL on a pro-rata basis.
- Excess Leave Utilization: If an employee leaves the organization after using more SL than entitled, the excess will be deducted from their gross salary.
- Leave Usage Rules: Employees can avail of half-day SL. For taking 3 or more days of SL at once, a medical certificate along with a fitness certificate is required. Employees must notify their Department Head, Superior, or HR Department within 24 hours of taking Sick Leave.
- Leave Clubbing: SL generally cannot be combined with PL, CL, Paternity Leave, or Compensatory Off. However, in cases of prolonged illness, PL and CL may be used in conjunction with SL if the employee has exhausted their SL balance.
- Intervening Days Off: Any weekly offs or paid holidays that occur during the SL period will be counted as SL.
## Casual Leave (CL):
- Leave Entitlement: Employees are entitled to 10 days of Sick Leave (SL) per year.
- Carry Forward Limit: Employees can carry forward a maximum of 20 days of SL each year, excluding the current year's entitlement.
- Leave Encashment: There is no provision for encashing SL.
- Leave Lapse: Any SL accumulated beyond 20 days will be forfeited.
- Leave Credit: SL will be credited at the start of each year.
- Pro-Rata Credit: Employees who join after January 1st will receive SL on a pro-rata basis.
- Excess Leave Utilization: If an employee leaves the organization after using more SL than entitled, the excess will be deducted from their gross salary.
- Leave Usage Rules: Employees can avail of half-day SL. For taking 3 or more days of SL at once, a medical certificate along with a fitness certificate is required. Employees must notify their Department Head, Superior, or HR Department within 24 hours of taking Sick Leave.
- Leave Clubbing: SL generally cannot be combined with PL, CL, Paternity Leave, or Compensatory Off. However, in cases of prolonged illness, PL and CL may be used in conjunction with SL if the employee has exhausted their SL balance.
- Intervening Days Off: Any weekly offs or paid holidays that occur during the SL period will be counted as SL.
## Maternity Leave (ML):
- Number of days per year - 26 weeks (As per the Maternity Act/or ESI Act). The Maternity Leave will be regulated by the Maternity Act or the ESI Act,1948.
- All the above leave is paid leave.
- Paternity leave is applicable to all permanent male employees.
- Employees are eligible for Two Paternity leave for first two days from date of Birth of Child.
- Paternity leave is applicable up to two children only.
## Additional Weekly off
- Deputy Manager and above employee provided two additional weekly off in a month. This is an additional off provided to ones in a week as per the government rules.
## Leave Without Pay
- LWP can be applied by an employee when no other leave is available or eligible. A maximum of 30 days of LWP can be availed on the approval of department head.
## SHIFT CHANGE:
- Monthly shift schedule should be assigned in Online system within 4 working days from the starting of every month.
- Three shift change can be considered in a month for only emergencies not for the routine personal activities which required prior approval of department Head through online system only.

chapters.title: Bonus:
chapters.text:
- Minimum Work Requirement: Employees must have worked at least 30 days during the year to be eligible for the bonus.
- Bonus Year: The bonus year runs from April 1st to March 31st.
- Salary Limit for Bonus Eligibility: The eligibility for receiving a bonus will be determined according to the Bonus Act. Employers are required to pay a minimum bonus of 8.33% of the employee's salary or basic wages, whichever is higher, for the accounting year.
- Eligibility Criteria: Employees with a basic salary of up to ₹10,000 are eligible for the bonus.
- Bonus Payment Deadline: The bonus must be paid within 8 months following the close of the accounting year.
- Bonus for Departing Employees: If an employee leaves during the current accounting year, their bonus will be paid along with the full and final settlement.

## Attendance Recording and Working Hours Policy
- Attendance Requirement: All employees are required to record their daily attendance to ensure accurate payroll processing. Attendance must be recorded using the Attendance Recording System (ARS) machines (Face Recognition/Touch Screen) available at all company locations, including factories and offices, according to shift timings. This policy aims to streamline the attendance process while fostering a culture of trust, integrity, and self-discipline within the organization.
- Recording Attendance: Employees must clock in and out at the designated times using ARS machines. In cases of power outages or technical issues with the ARS machines, employees must sign the attendance register, noting their in and out times.
- Punctuality Expectations: Employees are expected to be present at their workstations by the start of their shifts. Heads of Departments (HODs) are required to be seated for a minimum of 8 hours per day.
- Grace Period for Late Arrivals: A grace period of up to 15 minutes late is allowed three times a month to accommodate unavoidable delays such as traffic or personal matters. Beyond this, late arrivals will be marked as late, and leave (CL, SL, or PL) will be deducted. If no leave balance is available, it will be treated as Leave Without Pay (LWP). Employees should inform their managers or colleagues of any delays. Employees may arrive late or leave early by up to 2 hours, but no more than twice a month. Exceeding this limit will result in salary deductions or the requirement to apply for a half-day leave. This provision is intended for emergencies only and should not be misused.
- Minimum Attendance Requirement: To be counted as a half-day, employees must clock in at least 3.5 hours of attendance. Attendance less than 3.5 hours will be treated as a full-day absence, subject to the grace period rules. Arriving or leaving more than 2 hours late/early will result in a half-day absence.
- Official and Personal Work During Shift Hours: Employees leaving the office or factory during working hours for official or personal reasons must apply for a gate pass (Official Duty Gate Pass for official work and Personal Gate Pass for personal work) and swipe their attendance card or use the ARS to clock out and in when leaving and returning.
- Extended Official Duty: If an employee is on official duty outside the office/factory and cannot return before the end of office hours, they do not need to return solely to mark attendance. The employee can regularize their attendance the following day by getting their gate pass approved by their superior and then regularizing their attendance online with the superior’s approval.
- Travel Authorization: Employees on domestic, international, or out-of-headquarters travel will have their attendance authorized by the HR Department based on the approved Travel Indent Form. Such travel must be authorized by the respective HOD.
- Leave Planning: Employees should plan and apply for leave in advance before proceeding. Attendance must be regularized accordingly.
- Emergency Leave: In urgent situations where a leave application could not be submitted online before taking leave, the HR Department will accept the application up to four working days after the employee returns to work. Failure to submit within this time frame will result in the employee being marked as absent without pay.

chapters.title: Flexible working hours Policy
chapters.text:
- Eligibility for Flexible Working Hours: Flexible working hours are available to all full-time employees who have successfully completed their probationary period and have consistently demonstrated reliability and accountability in their roles.
- Core Working Hours Requirement: While flexibility is supported, employees are required to be present during core hours, from 09:00 AM to 5:30 PM, to ensure adequate team coverage and effective collaboration.
- Flexible Work Arrangements: Employees have the option to choose from various flexible work arrangements, including compressed workweeks, flexitime, or staggered shifts. These arrangements are subject to approval by their supervisor based on departmental needs.
- Remote Work Options: Telecommuting is available for eligible employees, allowing them to work remotely for part of their scheduled hours. This option requires approval and adherence to company policies and guidelines.
## Eligibility Criteria:
- Role Suitability: Roles identified as having 85% independent tasks (e.g., coding, data entry, content creation) and only 15% dependent on in-person interactions are deemed suitable for flexible working hours.
- Performance Criteria: Employees must have a minimum performance rating of "Good" or higher, quantitatively defined as scoring 3.5 or above on a 5-point scale in their latest performance evaluation, along with demonstrating less than a 2% error rate in task execution over the past 6 months.
- Formal Request Process: Employees wishing to adjust their working hours must submit a formal request to their supervisor, detailing their proposed schedule and the rationale for the change. Supervisors will evaluate requests based on operational needs and team dynamics.
- Communication & Coordination: Effective communication between employees and supervisors is crucial for maintaining smooth coordination and workflow continuity. Regular reviews of flexible working arrangements will be conducted to assess their effectiveness and address any emerging issues. Provisions will be made to ensure ongoing communication, such as regular check-ins and virtual meetings.

chapters.title: Overtime Policy
chapters.text:
- Eligibility: All non-managerial employees (below the executive level) are eligible for the Overtime policy, while management staff (executive level and above) are entitled to Compensatory Off as per the leave policy. For any questions about eligibility, please reach out to the HR Department.
- Overtime Requirements: Overtime will be recognized only after a minimum of 2.5 hours worked beyond regular working hours.
- Overtime Compensation: Overtime pay will be calculated according to local regulations, with double the employee's basic salary being paid for overtime hours.
- Logistical Arrangements: Employees are responsible for their own logistical arrangements. However, if the company’s facilities are available, they will be provided, but no special arrangements will be made.
- Departmental Responsibility: It is the responsibility of the Head of Department (HOD) to ensure smooth operations and minimize the use of overtime, adhering to legal requirements.
- Purpose of Overtime: Overtime is intended for tasks that are extra, urgent, or unexpected and is not linked to the department's regular productivity.
- Accrual of Overtime: Overtime accrues when a non-exempt employee works beyond the normal working hours on any given workday. Exceptions to this policy may be granted with top management approval.
## Terms and Conditions:
- All overtime worked must be approved in advance by the Head of Department. This request shall be in writing. Only in exceptional circumstances (e.g., a meeting with a client that runs late, a pressing deadline, Audit etc.) can this request be made at the last minute. The Head of department will evaluate last minute requests on a case-by-case basis. An employee who works overtime without prior approval may be subject to corrective action.
- Whenever feasible, efforts should be made to avoid accruing compensatory time by adjusting the employees' work hours within the same work week.
- Shift Change for Personal work cannot relate to Overtime.
## Remuneration process
## Purpose
The purpose of this policy is to ensure transparent, consistent, and effective communication of the Company’s remuneration framework to all employees. The policy aims to enable employees to clearly understand the structure, components, and principles governing their remuneration, beyond interactions with Human Resources personnel.
## Scope
This Remuneration Communication Policy is applicable across all Company employees, workers, contractors, sub-contractors, suppliers, and other stakeholders globally, including the communities in which the Company operates. It ensures that remuneration-related information is consistently communicated throughout all sites and operations, in compliance with applicable labour laws and internal governance standards.
## Statement
The Company is committed to maintaining a fair, transparent, and non-discriminatory remuneration system and ensuring that all employees are adequately informed about how their compensation is determined, structured, and reviewed.
Remuneration communication shall be clear, accessible, and understandable, allowing employees to comprehend the elements of their pay, including fixed and variable components, benefits, deductions, and statutory contributions.
## Remuneration Structure Communication
The Company ensures that employees receive clear information on their remuneration through the following mechanisms:
- Employment Contracts and Appointment Letters, which specify base salary, allowances, benefits, incentives (where applicable), payment frequency, and statutory contributions.
- Payslips, issued periodically, providing a detailed breakdown of earnings, deductions, and employer contributions.
- Employee Handbook and Internal Communication Materials, outlining the general remuneration framework, benefit eligibility, and compensation principles.
- Internal Notices, Circulars, or Digital Communications, used to communicate updates related to remuneration policies, statutory changes, or benefit structures.
## Salary Progression and Advancement
Where applicable, the Company communicates the principles governing salary progression and advancement, which may include:
- Performance-based reviews
- Role or grade progression
- Skill development and competency enhancement
- Tenure and experience
Employees are informed of the applicable review cycles and evaluation criteria through established internal communication channels.
## Equal Pay and Compliance
The Company ensures that remuneration practices:
- Comply with all applicable wage, labour, and employment laws
- Are free from discrimination based on gender, caste, religion, age, disability, or any other protected characteristic
- Align with minimum wage and statutory benefit requirements

- Coverage Details: The Group Personal Accident Insurance provides comprehensive protection for accidents that occur both during and outside of working hours, offering 24-hour coverage globally. This insurance covers potential outcomes such as death, permanent disability, or temporary disablement.
- Applicability: This policy applies to all employees of Jutify Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd., including permanent staff, trainees, and workmen who are on the company's payroll, ensuring risk coverage in the event of an accident.
- This Policy provides risk coverage in case of an accident of an employee by providing the following benefits:
- Medical Expenses Coverage: Reimbursement for medical expenses incurred due to treatment for permanent or total temporary disablement resulting from an accident.
- Accident Leave Compensation: Weekly compensation provided for time off work due to an accident, covering both temporary total disablement and permanent partial disablement as outlined in the Group Personal Accident (GPA) policy.
- Compensation for Death or Disablement: Financial compensation awarded to the nominated beneficiary in the event of an employee's death caused by an accident, or compensation to the employee in cases of permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement.
- Additional Benefits: Provision of other benefits as specified by the policy.
## Reimbursement and Benefit:
## Compensation Determination: The compensation amount and type will vary based on the level of disability sustained. The available reimbursements under the scheme include:
## Medical Expenses Reimbursement: Coverage for medical expenses related to treatment for temporary total disablement will be reimbursed in accordance with the insurance policy terms.
## Death Benefits: In the event of an employee's death due to an accident, the beneficiary or nominee will receive the full sum assured, as specified by the insurance policy.
## Permanent Disablement Benefits: For permanent disablement, benefits will be provided based on the nature of the disablement, as determined by the insurance authorities.
## Accident During Employment: If an employee is involved in an accident during work or while traveling to or from work, or on official business, and requires medical treatment and leave, the company will grant paid 'Accident Leave' and reimburse all medical expenses. Any insurance claim received for leave compensation and medical expenses will be retained by the company.
## Accident Outside Employment: If an accident occurs outside of employment or is unrelated to work, and the employee requires leave and medical treatment, the leave will be unpaid, and the employee will cover their own medical expenses. However, any insurance claim for leave compensation and medical expenses will be reimbursed to the employee according to the GPA policy.
## Additional Benefits: Other benefits are provided in accordance with the terms of the GPA policy from the insurance company.
## Policy Details: All benefits and claims procedures will adhere to the details outlined in the GPA policy. In case of any disputes or discrepancies regarding the policy terms or benefits, the original GPA policy issued by the insurance company will take precedence.
## Applicability: All Employee
- All employees are entitled to receive Gratuity based on their duration of service with the company.
- In the unfortunate event of an employee’s death or permanent total disability that leads to a complete loss of earning capacity, the Gratuity will be calculated based on the total length of service, as if the employee had continued to work until the actual date of retirement.
- Gratuity is calculated at the rate of 15 days' wages, using the most recent Basic Wages.
- Wages for this calculation include only Basic Wages and do not encompass additional allowances, overtime pay, commissions, or other terminal benefits.
- The Gratuity calculation formula is: [(Basic + DA + VDA) / 26 x 15 x Number of eligible years of service].
## Forfeiture:
- Partial: Where an employee’s service is terminated for causing damage or loss, wilfully or negligently, the gratuity may be forfeited to the extent of the damage or loss so caused.
- Total: Wholly forfeited if the services are terminated for riotous or disorderly conduct, any act of violence or offence of proved theft.

chapters.title: Grievance Redressal Procedure
chapters.text:
## Grievance Submission Process:
Employees should submit their grievance in writing to their manager, with a copy sent to the relevant department head. If the grievance involves the manager, the employee should still contact the manager directly and copy the concerned parties.
## Acknowledgment of Receipt:
The manager must promptly acknowledge receipt of the grievance in writing, notify the employee, and schedule a formal meeting.
## Review and Resolution:
For grievances related to the employee’s own function, the manager is responsible for reviewing and resolving the issue. If immediate resolution is not possible, the manager should commit to a timeline based on dependencies involving other departments or factors.
## Consultation:
If the grievance involves other departments or functions, the manager should consult with the relevant areas and provide a course of action or solution within 7 working days from receipt.
## Escalation:
Should the employee remain unsatisfied with the resolution, they may escalate the grievance to the department head or a member of the Leadership Team (LT), particularly if the grievance concerns the department head.
## Leadership Team Review:
The LT member will communicate their decision to the employee through the department manager within 5 days of receiving the grievance. If deemed necessary, the LT may refer the matter to the Grievance Resolution Committee.
The Grievance Resolution Committee will consist of a minimum of three members from the Leadership Team, the concerned department manager, and another manager not in the same reporting line. The committee will allow the aggrieved employee and the involved parties to present their concerns. It includes representatives from other teams to ensure a fair and efficient resolution.

- The Grievance Resolution Committee will give their recommendation to the LT within 4 working days. The LT will take a decision based on this recommendation and communicate their decision through the concerned department Manager to the aggrieved employee within 15 working days from commencement of inquiry
- Grievances will be treated with utmost confidentiality and sensitivity
- Human Resources shall maintain a record all grievances referred to the Grievance Resolution Committee, number of grievances settled/ pending and report to the Senior Management Team on a quarterly basis
## Gross misconduct
If an employee’s grievance uncovers gross misconduct by another employee, associate, or vendor of Jutify Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd., HR will take appropriate action while ensuring the complainant’s identity remains confidential and is not disclosed in any forum.
The following list is provided as examples and is not exhaustive. Any conduct not explicitly listed but equivalent to gross misconduct will be treated as such. The Leadership Team (LT), in consultation with the Grievance Redressal Committee, will determine what constitutes gross misconduct based on the specifics of each case:
- Fraudulent activities
- Intentional falsification of documents
- Embezzlement of funds
- Theft
- Acts of intimidation, harassment, threats, or violence
- Misuse or misappropriation of position or benefits
- Willful damage to organizational assets or those belonging to employees, partners, or other stakeholders
- Defamation or disparagement of the organization or its personnel
- Accepting or offering bribes or other illegal gratifications, including sexual favors
- Severe impairment due to alcohol or illegal drug use on the job or during working hours
- Major negligence resulting in unacceptable loss, damage, or injury
- Significant insubordination
- Unauthorized access to or manipulation of confidential company records or information
## Appeals
An employee seeking to appeal a disciplinary decision must submit their appeal within five working days. The Grievance Redressal Committee will review all appeals and provide recommendations to the Leadership Team (LT). In particularly serious cases, the LT may consult with the Board for further input. The final decision made by the LT will be communicated in writing to the employee by the relevant department Manager. During the appeal process, any disciplinary action taken will be reassessed.
Should an employee wish to appeal they must do so in writing to the appropriate manager within five working days of being informed in writing of the formal action.
